facts.text: Pittsfield earned the nickname “Pork Capital” of the Midwest thanks to a long‑standing pork‑packing industry that fed Chicago’s meat markets.
The city’s courthouse, built in 1855, remains a popular landmark that tourists often photograph while strolling the downtown square.
Pittsfield Public Library opened in 1855 with 40 members and 400 volumes, and it later received a $7,500 Carnegie grant to move into its current building in 1907.
The library’s digital archive hosts nearly 9,000 pages of historical newspapers, free for researchers and genealogy enthusiasts through Advantage Archives.
Pittsfield’s roots trace back to 1820 when settlers from Pittsfield, Massachusetts, crossed the Mississippi and established farms, roads, and the first government buildings.
In 2019, author Allen Carden and Thomas J. Ebert celebrated Pittsfield’s literary heritage with a book signing at the historic William Watson Hotel.
